key_insight: An EfficientNet-based deep learning model, especially EfficientNetB4 with additive attention, improved pediatric bone age prediction from hand X-rays compared with a smaller baseline model.
clinical_relevance: More accurate automated bone age estimation could support pediatric endocrine assessment by reducing manual workload and helping standardize image-based evaluation.
method: Trained on 12,000+ RSNA pediatric hand X-rays
Compared EfficientNetB0, EfficientNetB4, and EfficientNetB4 + Additive Attention
Used preprocessing to convert images into three-channel inputs for CNN learning
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that EfficientNetB4 and EfficientNetB4 with additive attention generally predicted bone age closer to the original age than EfficientNetB0, with learning curves suggesting stable training and validation.
watch_item: Performance should be validated across external hospitals and populations before clinical use, since dataset-specific results may not generalize everywhere.
paper_title: Pediatric Bone Age Prediction Using Deep Learning
